cases.name: Rectangular rooms: paired
cases.description: A small periodic exact cover of an ordinary tight grid is compiled into actual exclusive atomic ownership. Whole L/T/step/rectangular regions come from removing their internal shared edges, rather than independently placing possibly overlapping outlines.

stages.name: Atomic shared-edge field
stages.description: The small cells cover the supplied finite patch once each. Actual adjacent faces traverse one shared edge identity in opposite directions.

stages.name: Release selected repeated dividers
stages.description: A connected portion of every repeated cell is merged first. The other atomic faces remain separate; withdrawn internal edges remain in the transition witness.

stages.name: Complete the repeated interior shapes
stages.description: Remaining internal separators are withdrawn. Each complete tile owns its actual atomic faces exclusively; neighbouring interiors share their common boundary rather than independently drawing overlapping outlines.

stages.description: The small cells cover the supplied finite patch once each. Actual adjacent faces traverse one shared edge identity in opposite directions.

stages.name: Release selected repeated dividers
stages.description: A connected portion of every repeated cell is merged first. The other atomic faces remain separate; withdrawn internal edges remain in the transition witness.

stages.name: Complete the repeated interior shapes
stages.description: Remaining internal separators are withdrawn. Each complete tile owns its actual atomic faces exclusively; neighbouring interiors share their common boundary rather than independently drawing overlapping outlines.

stages.name: Complete the repeated interior shapes
stages.description: Remaining internal separators are withdrawn. Each complete tile owns its actual atomic faces exclusively; neighbouring interiors share their common boundary rather than independently drawing overlapping outlines.

cases.name: Negotiated broad seam: paired
cases.description: Neighbouring rectangular rooms independently request atomic faces along a broad step or shoulder. Their desired claims overlap, so an explicit actual-face decision is needed before the final shared seam can settle. Rejected claims remain inspectable.

stages.name: Atomic shared-edge field
stages.description: The small cells cover the supplied finite patch once each. Actual adjacent faces traverse one shared edge identity in opposite directions.

stages.name: Merge the rectangular starting rooms
stages.description: Repeated ordinary rectangles first absorb their atomic separators. The finite frontier is shown separately from the full interior occurrences.

stages.name: Expose the neighbours' incompatible offers
stages.description: Each side retains its current atoms and independently requests a broad shoulder of its neighbour. The offered interiors overlap, so these are blocked desired claims rather than a valid filled partition.

stages.name: Accept one common stepped seam
stages.description: Every contested actual face has an explicit chosen owner. The accepted and rejected side offers stay connected to the negotiation witness; only the resulting exclusive common boundary is rendered as the settled seam.

counterexamples.name: Unowned interior left as a gap

limits: Exclusive atomic occupancy and convex-atom embedding are separate checked premises, not arbitrary polygon boolean solving.
The finite field records complete translated tiles and its frontier; this is not recognition from pixels or an unbounded tiling theorem.
Shape-turn, proportion and boundary-detail diagnostics are authored preferences, not validated universal beauty laws.
Repeated atomic reach counts choose a construction resolution; no numeric carriers or measured lengths enter the source.
A native losing claim is blocked proposal evidence; observational conflict does not automatically become physical carrier tension.
